How can inventory fall without collapsing service?

A method-only case for segmenting inventory, service, constraints and availability before changing stock policy.

Anonymised case studyAuthor: Pupsi PhullPublished 20 September 2026Updated 21 September 20266 minute readSupply chain and inventory management
Evidence status: Identity anonymised. Every published number is valid and has been checked against its approved source, period, baseline and context.

Challenge

Aggregate stock can rise while customer availability deteriorates. A broad reduction target can remove the wrong inventory and increase expediting.

Diagnosis

Segment demand, lead time, lifecycle, constraint, customer promise and stock state. Distinguish physical stock from operationally available stock and trace where uncertainty enters.

Rebuild

Change policy by segment, test the service effect, make exceptions visible and verify the result at 30 and 90 days before scaling.

Questions for the reader

  • Which inventory is unavailable despite being physically present?
  • Where is buffer compensating for unreliable lead time or data?
  • Which service definition must be protected?
  • What evidence would stop the reduction?
